sections.overview: Pinirampus pirinampu is a South American freshwater catfish in the family Pimelodidae.
sections.identification: It is a large river catfish known locally in parts of Brazil as barba-chata.
sections.habitat: It occurs in major South American river systems, including the Amazon, Orinoco, Essequibo and Paraná basins.
sections.diet: Although often described as a fish-eating predator, a recent study in the Xingu found aquatic insects dominant in stomach contents, while isotope results indicated assimilated resources from fish, crustaceans and molluscs.
sections.behavior: It is reported as nocturnal and moves within river systems; field work in the Xingu also describes foraging both in the water column and near the bottom.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive details were not established by the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: Its feeding evidence shows that prey use can vary by study method and river setting, so the Xingu findings should not be treated as a universal diet.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern, dated 2020.
